mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 100k indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k, or the rank correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and corporate margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with UNRATE below 7.5% for two consecutive months, or the average return in triggered months is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1% indicates robust economic activity across consumer and business sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both HOUST and INDPRO rise by at least 1%, or the interaction term in a regression model is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97.0 signals weakening economic momentum, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months with FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and INDPRO < 97.0, or the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and INDPRO is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2% indicates moderate inflation that supports economic growth and corporate pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with CPIAUCSL growth exceeding 0.2%, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL growth and SPX returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% signals imminent monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates on equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months with FEDFUNDS rising above 0.25%, or the average return in triggered months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) and non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% indicates strong consumer demand and labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both HOUST and PAYEMS rise by at least 0.5%, or the interaction term in a regression model is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime, housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 760,000 units signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with HOUST > 760.0 during post-recession recovery, or the average return in triggered months is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).
